title: Fourth moment of a product polynomial
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let each $\Omega_i$ for $i\in\mathrm{Fin}\ n$ be finite, and choose a probability mass function $p_i$ on each $\Omega_i$ and a function $X_i:\Omega_i\to\mathbb{R}$. Suppose each $X_i$ has mean zero and third moment zero under $p_i$, and is reasonable with constant $B$. For coefficients $a_S\in\mathbb{R}$ indexed by subsets $S\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}\ n$, suppose $a_S=0$ whenever $|S|>k$. Then under the independent product distribution of the $p_i$, the fourth moment of the associated multilinear random variable is at most $\max(B,9)^k$ times the square of its second moment.
hypotheses_covered: $n\ge 0$ and each coordinate space $\Omega_i$ is finite
Each coordinate third moment is zero
Each coordinate is reasonable with constant $B$
Coefficients vanish on subsets of size greater than $k$
